title: With flagship models
question: Does adding 3 flagship models to the pool pay off?

flagships.data_policy: OpenRouter paid route pinned to OpenAI (standard tier).
OpenRouter paid route pinned to Google AI Studio (standard tier).
OpenRouter paid route pinned to Moonshot AI (its own MXFP4 deployment).

excluded_flagships.reason: Stopped on 2026-11-14 after 375 of 900 prompts. Its reasoning ignored the 4,096-token answer limit on knowledge questions (one answer ran to 35,234 tokens and ten minutes), so finishing would have taken the flagship runs past their $25 budget.

router.selection_rule: Lower validation log loss between logistic regression and gradient-boosted trees, as the proposal specifies; the train-to-validation gap is the overfitting check.

protocol: The flagships (GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Carbon, Kimi K3.1 Pro) answered the 600 suite prompts and the 300 fresh prompts on 2026-11-14 through OpenRouter, each pinned to its maker's own standard tier, with the same prompts, token limits, retry policy, and grading as the Checkpoint 3 pool.

Grok 4.7 is left out: Stopped on 2026-11-14 after 375 of 900 prompts. Its reasoning ignored the 4,096-token answer limit on knowledge questions (one answer ran to 35,234 tokens and ten minutes), so finishing would have taken the flagship runs past their $25 budget.

The second router uses the Checkpoint 3 recipe unchanged on all 12 models: classifier family and regularization chosen on validation log loss, presets tuned on the validation split with the same grids and accuracy floors, then refit on train + validation.
The strongest flagship, Gemini 4 Carbon, is the one with the most right answers on the train and validation prompts, fixed before the test and fresh results were read.

The paired comparisons were fixed in code before the flagships' results were read; p-values are Holm-adjusted within each evaluation. Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over prompts (10,000 resamples, fixed seed).
The fresh prompts were already used once, to evaluate the frozen router. Nothing in this extension was chosen on them; they are read once more here.

evaluations.title: Original test split
evaluations.description: The 120 held-out test prompts of the 600-prompt suite, answered by the Checkpoint 3 pool in late October and by the flagships on 2026-11-14.

comparisons.question: Does the best-quality setting get more right with the flagships in the pool?
Is the best-quality setting as accurate as always using the strongest flagship, for less?
Does adding the flagships change the lowest-cost setting?
Does adding the flagships change the fastest setting?
Does the balanced setting do better with the flagships in the pool?
With the flagships, do the prompt features add accuracy beyond per-task averages?
